analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains
key_insights: GS baseline for 2027 is stable global growth, declining inflation and peaking policy rates, but market-cycle risks skew to the downside: real rates are higher, credit spreads wider and volatility is rising under the surface. GS argues for more diversified, better-hedged portfolios including bonds.

The AI investment impulse (additional AI investment as a share of GDP) is forecast to peak in early 2027, with the investment share itself peaking in 2028. GS sees this as manageable for the economy but a bigger test for markets, because AI contributed far more to earnings and market value growth than to GDP growth.
AI infrastructure beneficiaries have already de-rated since June. The open question is whether record S&P 500 earnings relative to GDP prove persistent as the investment cycle fades.
S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. GS says this should limit the de-rating of AI-exposed areas but also means less relief in core rates pricing.

Equity leadership may pass from AI infrastructure to hyperscalers (if monetization becomes visible), AI-productivity users and non-AI companies as capital crowding-out eases. The risk is that the handoff is slow or that tighter financial conditions turn a rotation into a broader market shock. GS sees financial conditions as the most likely channel for AI worries to hit the economy.

An escalation-driven oil spike from the Iran war is one of the largest near-term risks. Oil has fallen in November and pricing is vulnerable to broader conflict or new supply disruptions. The baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices. Europe faces a precarious winter because natural gas storage is low.

Oil risk premium was very high at the end of October and has since fallen. When the premium is low, energy's hedge value is higher. When it is high, outright longs are riskier than options. Faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine would be a major upside risk for equities and bonds.

Bonds: GS sees central bank pricing as too hawkish in the US and UK relative to its baseline, and expects policy rates to peak lower and reverse earlier than in 2023-2024. Duration is favored on running yield, cheap valuations (UST 10y forecast 4.6% at end-2027), underweight positioning and paths to shallow rate relief. Bonds are already hedging better, with Bunds rallying as French spreads widened and USTs rallying as tech fell.

Dollar: GS expects the broad trade-weighted Dollar to fall about 3% in 2027 as US inflation converges to target, energy declines and the Fed moves from hikes to cuts in late 2027 and early 2028. The Fed shift is expected as 2027 ends and 2028 begins.

If US tech performance erodes, GS expects the Dollar to underperform cyclically rather than get a safe-haven bid. The undervalued Yen would be the better haven, with Japanese authorities focused on limiting Yen weakness. GS also sees gradual CNY appreciation given undervaluation and a growing trade surplus.

Europe is under pressure from the terms-of-trade shock, higher global yields and French sovereign stress. Fiscal issues in France are unlikely to be addressed before the spring 2027 French election, so EUR downside optionality stays attractive and EUR remains a popular funder. Relief mostly comes through global channels (lower energy, lower core yields), and a slower AI spend would favor Europe given its smaller tech weight.

UK: Gilts have the highest beta to oil, so they are the clearest beneficiary of lower oil. UK equities are defensive with low tech exposure but significant energy exposure. Sterling is the most overvalued G10 currency by GS's measure and GS's monetary policy forecasts are the most dovish relative to market pricing in the UK, so further gains are harder.

Credit: record credit and equity issuance to fund AI investment has been digestible at discounted pricing, and AI-related credit has underperformed in the last 6 months. GS expects modest further widening in US index spreads in 2027, with risks skewed to wider. It expects modest US HY underperformance (decompression). Europe offers more risk premium, and mortgages and structured credit offer refuge from corporate supply.

EM assets showed resilience in 2026, but valuations are less compelling: local spreads are tight, EM credit spreads are the tightest in years, and FX carry is mid-range. GS favors exposure to high, diversified yields in hard- and local-currency bonds (South Africa, Hungary, Colombia, India named) and, in equities, a diversified earnings mix, especially equal-weighted indices.

GS baseline forecasts positive 2027 returns for equities and bonds. Tail hedges it highlights: lower US and Japan rates, USD/JPY downside, TTF call spreads and European gas futures, EUR funding, out-of-the-money equity puts, or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated calls.
Equity index volatility has risen a little but is unlikely to fall much and has scope to rise if macro stresses broaden. The sharpest volatility so far is under the surface of the major indices.

sector_views.rationale: Already de-rated since June. The AI investment impulse peaks in early 2027, so the focus shifts to whether record profits persist.
Defensive, with less tech exposure than the US. The significant energy weight is a offsetting factor.
Pressured by energy terms of trade and French stress, but a smaller tech share would look relatively better if AI spending slows.
Diversified earnings mix across North Asia tech, South Africa and LatAm cyclicals and India domestic demand. Equal-weighted indices preferred.
Heavy AI-related issuance needs discounted pricing, and spreads are likely to widen, with risks skewed wider.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth decelerating from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027 (forecast, GS estimate).
S&P 500 total earnings are at a record share of GDP (GS Exhibit 2, 4-quarter moving average).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Deceleration but still robust growth should limit the de-rating of AI-exposed areas and imply less relief in core rates pricing.
GS regards current valuations as cheap and sees paths to shallow rate relief under the baseline.
Lower inflation, lower energy prices and a Fed shift from hikes to cuts support a softer Dollar.

macro_indicators.reading: Move from hikes to cuts into late 2027 and early 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is seen as too hawkish relative to this path.

macro_indicators.reading: Peaks in early 2027; investment share peaks in 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: The second-derivative peak limits upside for AI-exposed equities even while growth stays positive.
Risks are skewed to wider, with AI-related issuers underperforming everything else.

trade_ideas.description: Position for lower rates in the US and Japan, or jointly lower rates and equities, as a hedge against deeper downside growth tails
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth risks skew to the downside and a growing number of risks would push both growth and rate expectations lower.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher oil prices or sticky core inflation would push rates higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD/JPY downside (short USD/JPY) as a hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: USD/JPY generally performs well when rates and equities both fall, and Japanese authorities are limiting Yen weakness.

trade_ideas.description: European gas futures and TTF call spreads, plus EUR funding, as asymmetric hedges against energy risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Europe faces a precarious winter with low gas storage, vulnerable to supply and weather risks.

trade_ideas.description: Buy out-of-the-money equity puts, or replace equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Deeper protection is more valuable than usual as the market cycle matures.
French fiscal issues persist until the spring 2027 election, and the skew of risks and low carry favor downside optionality.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy or global yield relief could support Europe.

trade_ideas.description: Own CNY and JPY appreciation (Asia's revaluing currencies) against the Dollar
trade_ideas.rationale: China's trade surplus is growing and the Yuan is deeply undervalued. The Yen is an attractive hedge to pro-cyclical portfolios.
trade_ideas.risk: Very weak domestic demand in China.

trade_ideas.rationale: Higher running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and paths to rate relief.
trade_ideas.risk: Extended energy shock or stickier inflation with a resilient labour market.

trade_ideas.description: Favor EM local and hard-currency bonds and equal-weighted EM equities for diversified yield and earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: High, diversified yields with improving fiscal stories in South Africa, Hungary, Colombia and India.
trade_ideas.risk: Tight spreads and middle-of-the-road carry leave less valuation cushion.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Iran war driving an oil spike while equities and bonds are both under pressure.
Europe's low natural gas storage leaves supply and weather risk this winter.
A sharper AI boom reversal, or AI-related drawdowns tightening financial conditions.
The baton pass from AI infrastructure to other areas of the market does not happen on time.
Sticky core inflation or a resilient labour market keeping rates higher.
Jumbo AI debt issuance causing episodic indigestion and wider credit spreads, with weaker borrowers in the left tail.
French fiscal and sovereign stress ahead of the spring 2027 election.
Erosion of US tech exceptionalism undermining the Dollar's premium valuation.

Exhibit 7: The 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y US Treasury correlation, based on ES and TY futures, from Dec-25 to Nov-26, which GS says shows more negative equity-bond correlations and improved hedging value of bonds.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little but is unlikely to fall much from here and has scope to rise if macro stresses broaden. The sharpest volatility has been under the surface of major indices.
Bond positioning is underweight per GS.
EUR has been a popular funding currency, and GS sees low carry and the skew of risks keeping downside optionality attractive.
Out-of-the-money equity puts, or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options, are seen as more valuable than usual as the cycle matures.
TTF call spreads and European gas futures are suggested as asymmetric hedges against energy upside.
The 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y UST correlation has turned more negative in 2026, improving bonds' hedging value (Exhibit 7).
geopolitical: Iran war: another escalation could spike oil and hurt equities, support the Dollar against European currencies and push rates up. Oil supply has largely been restored.
Ukraine: faster progress toward resolution is named as a source of upside risk for broader markets, since lower energy prices would support bonds and equities.
French election in spring 2027: French fiscal issues are unlikely to be adequately addressed before it, which keeps EUR downside attractive.
Houthi blockade announcement, ceasefire and MoU signing are annotated as drivers of the Brent risk premium in Exhibit 6.
Japanese authorities are focused on limiting further Yen depreciation and encouraging inflows into Japanese assets.
US midterms are annotated on the Brent risk premium chart in Exhibit 6.

tension_points.theme: AI capex peak and market baton pass
tension_points.bull_case: AI investment and earnings stay firmly positive in 2027 (S&P 500 earnings +11%), and leadership passes to hyperscalers, AI users and non-AI companies as capital crowding-out eases.
tension_points.bear_case: The baton pass is slow or the market looks ahead to the 2028 peak in the investment share, and tighter financial and credit conditions turn a rotation into a larger aggregate shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tighter financial or credit conditions feeding back faster than the baseline, or other market areas failing to take up the slack as AI infrastructure flattens.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices as supply recovers, and faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine would support bonds and equities.
tension_points.bear_case: An escalation in the Iran war or new supply disruptions could spike oil, hurting equities and possibly bonds together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another escalation of the Iran war or broader supply disruption would invalidate the gradual-decline baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Central bank pricing is too hawkish, policy rates peak lower and reverse earlier, and bonds offer running yield and hedge value.
tension_points.bear_case: The energy shock extends, inflation stays sticky and the labour market stays resilient, pushing rates higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extended energy shock or stickier inflation with a resilient labour market.

theme_stances.evidence: may be a bigger test for markets for three reasons
